```{r, include = FALSE}
# The build needs a MOSPI API key and network access, so no chunk runs.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The package does not include the survey microdata. You download the
microdata one time from the MOSPI microdata portal (catalog 255, dataset
`DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSS-CMSE80-2025`). Then you build a data directory of Parquet
files. All the query functions of the package read this directory.

You can do the build from R or from the command line. The two methods run
the same code.

## Before you start

1. Get an API key from <https://microdata.gov.in>.

2. Add the key to `~/.Renviron`:

   ```
   MOSPI_KEY=your-key-here
   ```

3. Start R again. R reads the key when it starts.

4. Install the packages for the build:

   ```{r}
   install.packages("mospiR", repos = c("https://saketlab.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
   install.packages(c("arrow", "haven", "readxl"))
   ```

## The data directory

All the functions use one data directory. The default directory is
`tools::R_user_dir("educationsurveyindia", "data")`.

To use a different directory, set the `esi.data_dir` option in `~/.Rprofile`:

```{r}
options(esi.data_dir = "~/data/education")
```

`esi_build()`, `esi_download()`, `esi_download_all()`, `esi_connect()`, and
`esi info` use this option. In this article, `<data dir>` is the data directory.

## Build from R

```{r}
library(educationsurveyindia)
esi_build()
```

```
#> ℹ Downloading "DDI-IND-MOSPI-NSS-CMSE80-2025" from microdata.gov.in...
#> Downloaded: <data dir>/raw/Data in STATA.zip (8,493,471 bytes)
#> Downloaded: <data dir>/raw/CODEs for Blocks of Sch - CMS-Education.xlsx (19,480 bytes)
#> ℹ Reading 'CMSE80HH25.dta'
#> ✔  "household": 52085 rows, 33 cols
#> ℹ Reading 'CMSE80PER25.dta'
#> ✔  "person": 221617 rows, 40 cols
#> ℹ Reading 'CMSE80PERST25.dta'
#> ✔  "person_erstwhile": 1675 rows, 30 cols
#> ✔ Build complete. Output: '<data dir>'
```

The download is approximately 8.5 MB. After the download, the build is
complete in less than one minute.

To write the data to a different directory, use `output_dir`:

```{r}
esi_build(output_dir = "/data/cmse")
```

### Download only

`esi_download()` downloads and extracts the raw files. It does not build
the Parquet files.

```{r}
esi_download()                  # into <data dir>/raw
esi_download("/data/cmse/raw")
```

### Use files that you downloaded

If you downloaded `Data in STATA.zip` from the portal, set `raw_dir` to its
directory. The directory can also contain the extracted `.dta` files. An
API key is not necessary for this method.

```{r}
esi_build(raw_dir = "~/Downloads/cmse")
```

Put `CODEs for Blocks of Sch - CMS-Education.xlsx` in the same directory.
This codebook gives the correct value labels. If the codebook is missing,
the build uses the STATA value labels and shows a warning. Some STATA value
labels are not correct, for example the labels of `sector`.

## Download all the education rounds

CMS-E is the newest of seven NSS education surveys on the portal.
`esi_surveys()` shows the seven surveys:

```{r}
esi_surveys()
```

`esi_download_all()` downloads all the files of each round. The files are
the microdata in each format, the DDI codebook, the questionnaires, the
reports, and the code lists. Each round goes into `<data dir>/rounds/`.

```{r}
res <- esi_download_all()                 # all rounds, less than 1 GB
esi_download_all(rounds = c("64", "75"))  # only these rounds
res$missing                               # the files that did not download
```

The function does not download a file again if the file is on your
computer. Thus, if a download stops, run the function again. It downloads
only the missing files.

The portal API cannot give the files of the 52nd round. The dataset ID of
this round ends with a period, and the API does not accept this ID. Download
this round from catalog page 82 of the portal.

Only the 80th round can become Parquet files. The other rounds stay as raw files.

## Build from the command line

The package installs a script with the name `esi`. To use the script,
make a link to it in a directory on your `PATH`:

```{bash}
ln -s "$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("exec", "esi", package = "educationsurveyindia"))')" ~/.local/bin/esi
```

Then use these commands:

```{bash}
esi build                              # download if necessary, then build
esi build --output-dir /data/cmse      # build into a different directory
esi build --raw-dir ~/Downloads/cmse   # use files that you downloaded
esi download                           # download and extract only
esi info                               # show the tables that you built
esi help
```

`esi info` shows the tables and the row counts:

```
#> ✔ Connected to CMS-E data in '<data dir>'
#> ℹ 3 tables registered
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   table_name       n_records n_states
#>   <chr>                <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 household            52085       36
#> 2 person_erstwhile      1675       34
#> 3 person              221617       36
```

If you do not make the link, use `Rscript` to run the same commands:

```{bash}
Rscript -e 'educationsurveyindia::esi_cli()' build
```

The command line reads the API key only from `MOSPI_KEY`. There is no
`--api-key` option. Thus the key does not go into your shell history or the
process list.

If a command does not complete correctly, the exit status is 1. Thus you can use the commands in
scripts, for example `esi build && Rscript analysis.R`.

## Build again

The build does not download a raw file again if the file is in the raw
directory. Thus a second `esi_build()` or `esi build` only builds the
Parquet files again.

To download new copies of the files, use `overwrite`. Do this if MOSPI
changes the data, or if a download stopped before the end.

```{r}
esi_build(overwrite = TRUE)
```

```{bash}
esi build --overwrite
```

## The output files

The build writes these files:

```
<data dir>/
├── household.parquet
├── person.parquet
├── person_erstwhile.parquet
├── labels.duckdb            # variable labels and value labels
└── raw/                     # downloaded zip file, codebook, .dta files
```

The build adds two columns to each table:

- `weight`: the final survey weight, `mult / 100`.
- `state`: the NSS state code, the first two digits of `nss_region`.

## Connect to the data

```{r}
con <- esi_connect()
esi_available_data(con)
esi_disconnect(con)
```

To try the functions without the microdata, use `esi_example_data()`. This
function writes a very small synthetic data directory:

```{r}
con <- esi_connect(esi_example_data())
esi_expenditure_by_state(con)
esi_disconnect(con)
```
